why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests that clamp is exported (`typeof` is `function`) and that it returns values limited to lo..hi: below the range gives lo, above gives hi, inside or at a bound gives x. Any correct clamp gives those outputs, so the line's words force each one. Check 2 needs only a RangeError on three lo>hi inputs. Check 3 lists the exports at the head and needs README documentation "naming it with what it does" for each one, which is what "documents" means. Check 4 needs only exit status 0 and no failing tests. The stricter items (tests that cover clamp, clamp(5,5,5), the README mentioning RangeError) are all under "Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL)". No check requires a mutation test, a file-scope rule or exact wording.
